title: E-flat clarinet and low piccolo in I Want to Live!
summary: Mandel explains the chilling E-flat clarinet and low-register piccolo in the gas chamber scene, and instruments played out of register, which the players liked.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You used it really effectively in, I Want to Live!
I wanted a chilling sound and it's a chilling sound. It's not a warm sound, but it’s perfect for what it is.
That comes to mind, there was that segment, the gas chamber scene where you use the low register piccolo playing.
Right, how do you know that?
Did I write about it in the notes or something?
Or maybe, there’s a little bit of it in there about Harry Klee playing it I think.

Yeah… the low register piccolo is interesting ‘cause like low register flutes there are no, absolutely no, overtones to the bottom octave of those instruments. So it makes them sound an octave lower than they are, but also a low register piccolo sounds like a dying man gasping for breath, it's a very strange sound and it's not something you’d associate with a piccolo. In fact, on I Want to Live! I wrote all the instruments a great deal of the time way out of their registers either the high ones are playing very low or the low ones are playing very high. That was another effect I was trying to get, to try and submerge the identity of the instrument.
How did the players react to all these unconventional uses of their instruments?
They said, “Jesus, are you crazy,” no, they didn’t say that. [laughs] They were all for it, they liked it, they felt like they were doing something at the time.
It was definitely not a run in the mill film date.

I guess not. You know I don't have perspective of a player ever because I don’t have to sit day after day and play lots of different kinds of music. I'm in my own head and I know what I'm going to do, or if I don't know what I’m going to do I’ll know what I've done by the time I get into the date. And I have no idea what they've looked at that day from other people or what they've had to look at all week and so I figure if they don't throw me out of there I am doing pretty good.
